column2: # Mars' mean radius in meters, for geosphere distances
# spatial join output from ArcGIS (one row per basin-crater pair)
# field names got cut to 10 characters on export:
# DIAM_CIRC_ = crater diameter (km), LAT_CIRC_I = crater center lat, correct_lo = crater center lon (-180 to 180)
# keep the crater whose center is closest to the basin center as long as the basin is within half that crater's radius
# distance from basin center to crater center (Haversine, Mars' radius)
# how far off center the basin is, as a fraction of the crater's radius
select(basin_id, crater_id = CRATER_ID, crater_diam_km = DIAM_CIRC_, crater_offset_km)
# Fassett & Head lake numbers = Goudge open basin numbers
# turning lake area into a diameter as if the lake were a circle: area = pi * r^2, so d = 2 * sqrt(area / pi)
# lake size is the actual extent of the water, so prioritize using it (if a basin has one) over crater diameter
# if we can't find a basin's size, use the median radius of the basins that do have one
# (has to come after the combine step, since that's where basin_diam_km gets made)
# search radius for the hydrous minerals: half the basin diameter, or the median radius if there's no size
